title: Derived internal Hom and evaluation under an isomorphism of coefficient sites
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, with $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the coefficient-stage operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ take arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. At integral coefficients $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ take $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; the coefficient sheaf is the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. At $E$ take the localized operations on such integral objects, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ take their common finite-field representatives. Write $P=Lg^*$, $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ and $\mu:P(U\otimes^L V)\xrightarrow{\sim}PU\otimes^L PV$ for the canonical tensor comparison.

The evaluation-defined comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{g;M,N}:PH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(PM,PN).$$
It is characterized by the equality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{PM,PN}\circ(1_{PM}\otimes c_{g;M,N})\circ\mu_{M,H(M,N)}=P(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}).$$
It preserves tensor-Hom transposition: the transpose of $P(b)\circ\mu_{M,L}^{-1}$, for $b:M\otimes^L L\to N$, is $c_{g;M,N}\circ P(b^\sharp)$. These comparisons commute with the canonical cohomological shift identifications and with composition of scheme isomorphisms. At integral coefficients the pullback is identified with the exact inverse-image equivalence on completed module sheaves; its comparison with the tower-defined pullback is the canonical comparison commuting with all reduction projections. The tensor and evaluation comparisons are actual natural maps on the derived categories of reduction systems and their functorial derived-limit realizations, with their specified system evaluation and transposition maps [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; their identities hold there, rather than being inferred from equality of separately evaluated finite-level maps. At the two field stages the displayed maps and identities are the localized and common-stage images, natural also for arbitrary morphisms in the localized Hom groups.

proof.text:
Put $F=g^{-1}$, using the covering-preserving equivalence $(U\to X)\mapsto(U\to X\xrightarrow gY)$. Its quasi-inverse is inverse image along $g^{-1}$. Thus $F$ is exact, preserves products and coproducts, and identifies constant finite coefficient sheaves, compatibly with every quotient map. Also
$F\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=F\lim_n(A_{E,n})_Y\cong\lim_n(A_{E,n})_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$.
This is the actual comparison induced by all the projections. Reindexing sheaves and their module actions gives mutually inverse module equivalences for these completed ring sheaves as well: the inverse coefficient map is obtained by the same construction for $g^{-1}$ and their composites are identities on every projection. The tensor and sheaf-Hom comparisons are those on local sections, $s\otimes t\mapsto Fs\otimes Ft$ and $f\mapsto Ff$.

proof.text: These equivalences preserve the resolution classes directly. If $I$ is K-injective and $A$ is acyclic, a chain map $A\to FI$ corresponds under the inverse exact equivalence to a map $F^{-1}A\to I$; its null homotopy transports back. If $Q$ is K-flat, then $A\otimes FQ\cong F(F^{-1}A\otimes Q)$ is acyclic. Flat terms are preserved by the same argument on short exact sequences. Exactness carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and termwise application descends to the derived categories with the specified shift comparison. The termwise unit and counit still give inverse derived equivalences. At finite coefficients this derived functor is exactly $P=Lg^*$ in the question.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text:
For finite coefficients, and separately in the ambient completed-ring module category, choose a representative $K$ of $M$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$. In Hom degree $r$ the sheaf comparisons of Step 1 give
$F\prod_p\mathcal Hom(K^p,I^{p+r})\cong\prod_p\mathcal Hom(FK^p,FI^{p+r})$.
They commute with $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^r f d_K$, so define an isomorphism of Hom complexes. Step 2 makes $FI$ an admissible K-injective representative. Consequently localization gives an isomorphism $c:FH(M,N)\cong H(FM,FN)$. Naturality holds on maps of complexes, and independence of representatives and descent in both variables follow from the cited quasi-isomorphism invariance of Hom complexes. In particular this covers arbitrary unbounded finite-coefficient inputs.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text:
The cited internal currying isomorphism, followed by global-Hom recovery, gives the tensor-Hom transposition bijection. Use flat-term K-flat representatives for the tensor inputs. The canonical tensor comparison $\mu$ is induced by the ordinary comparison on their total tensor complexes. Evaluation is ordinary Hom-complex evaluation followed by the inverse localized augmentation of the target. Reindexing the pure-tensor evaluation $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$ gives the same chain map on either side. When evaluation is written in the order $x\otimes f$, both sides use the same Koszul symmetry. Thus
$\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1\otimes c)\mu=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})$.
The closed adjunction and its representative normalization identify this $c$ with the evaluation-defined comparison; the transposition bijection makes it the unique map satisfying this equation.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text:
For $b:M\otimes^L L\to N$ write $b=\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(1\otimes b^\sharp)$. Apply $F$ and the naturality of $\mu$. Step 4 gives
$F(b)\mu_{M,L}^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1\otimes(cF(b^\sharp)))$.
Applying the inverse of the transposition bijection proves the displayed transposition formula. It also proves naturality in $M,N$: after uncurrying either side of the naturality square one obtains the same composite of evaluation with the two input maps.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: The shift comparison for $F$ is identity in each degree. The Hom-complex identifications for $H(M[a],N[b])$ reindex the factors and multiply by the usual signs coming from $d_{K[a]}=(-1)^a d_K$. Step 3 applies $F$ to the same factors and the same integer signs, so its square with each of these identifications commutes as a square of complexes. It therefore commutes in the derived category. This checks shifts in both Hom inputs, rather than only a shift of the output.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: For a second scheme isomorphism $h:Z\to X$, identify $P_{gh}$ with $P_hP_g$ by the canonical derived pullback-composition map. The two candidate internal-Hom comparisons become equal after uncurrying: both give $P_hP_g(\operatorname{ev})$, since the tensor-composition square in the cited statement commutes. Injectivity of transposition proves the composition identity for $c$. For the identity scheme map it similarly gives the identity comparison. This is also visible before localization: two successive reindexings send a local homomorphism $f$ to $h^{-1}g^{-1}f$ in either construction.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text:
Now work integrally. For a derived-complete input $K$, the canonical quotient-tower unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YK$ is an isomorphism: apply the finite-free completed-scalar comparison with $L=E$. In particular this is the canonical unit, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism with a Roos triangle. Reindexing takes each reduction to the corresponding reduction of $FK$ and commutes with its quotient maps. It commutes with total derived inverse limit: apply it termwise to a K-injective resolution in the abelian tower category; Step 2's null-homotopy argument applies to tower maps, and the ordinary limit commutes with this equivalence. Hence
$F\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YK\cong\mathcal L_X F_\bullet\mathcal R_YK=Lg^*K$.
Composing with $F(u_K)$ gives the claimed natural identification $FK\cong Lg^*K$, with all its reduction projections fixed.

proof.text: The same calculation applied to the actual strict tensor-reduction complexes identifies $F(M\widehat\otimes^L N)$ with $FM\widehat\otimes^L FN$. On a flat-term K-flat model it reindexes each total-tensor summand, and on the Roos realization it reindexes both product coordinates and $1-s$. This is the specified completed tensor comparison, since that comparison is fixed by precisely these representative and Roos-coordinate equations. Coefficient transitions commute before taking the limit. The comparison is invertible, with inverse given by inverse reindexing. Substitution of normalized tensor/pullback systems shows that composition, symmetry, and shift comparisons have the same normalization after realization.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text:
To check integral evaluation against completed tensor, use the completion reflector. The constant-completion comparison identifies quotient-tower completion with Koszul completion, respecting its unit. The reflector then gives, for a complete target $N$,
$\operatorname{Hom}(\widehat{M\otimes^LL},N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes^LL,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,H(M,N))$.
Here the hat is the functorial completion of the ordinary tensor; its quotient tower is exactly the defining tower of completed tensor. Thus evaluation for completed tensor is the unique extension of ordinary evaluation along the completion unit. This establishes transposition on the complete full subcategory without assuming that ordinary tensor is already complete or that $M$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: Use the ambient completed-ring Hom comparison of Step 3. Under Step 8 it is the required integral $c$. Its source is constructible by the hypothesis on $H(M,N)$ and preservation of the integral category by pullback; hence its target is constructible as well. Precompose its completed evaluation equation with the ordinary-to-completed tensor unit. By Steps 4 and 9 this becomes the already proved ordinary evaluation equation. The reflector's bijection in Step 10 proves equality of the completed maps. Step 5 now proves the integral transposition formula; Steps 6 and 7 prove the shift and composition identities, since completion units and both Roos coordinates commute with reindexing. The hypothesis on the internal Hom is used here to stay on the stated constructible domain, not to obtain its ambient comparison.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: For the system assertion, reindex the underlying site while keeping the inverse-sequence index and all coefficient quotient arrows. This defines an exact equivalence of the two abelian categories of strict module systems, with an explicit inverse. Step 2 therefore applies to their unbounded derived categories. On their ringed sequence topoi, the product-Hom-complex construction of Step 3 gives an actual internal-Hom comparison and Step 4 gives an actual equality of evaluation maps. For cartesian first inputs its evaluations are the finite-level comparisons, by the fiberwise-Hom identification in the cited semilinear-system statement. In the transition formula of that statement, reindexing commutes with scalar extension, $t^M$, its inverse, $t^N$, and evaluation; consequently it gives the same transpose. Thus the maps respect the specified system transitions, before evaluation at any level.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: The comparison with integral reduction is the square having top $\mathcal R_X(FH(M,N))\to\mathcal R_XH(FM,FN)$ and bottom $F_\bullet\mathcal I_Y(\mathcal R_YM,\mathcal R_YN)\to\mathcal I_X(\mathcal R_XFM,\mathcal R_XFN)$, with vertical maps the specified $\beta$ and the canonical reduction/reindexing identifications. This square commutes as a system square: $\beta$ is defined by the same evaluation, and Step 12's reindexing carries that evaluation chain map and its transpose to themselves. Its unit/counit comparisons are the reduction/limit adjunction's actual unit and counit, so applying the functorial $\mathcal L$ preserves this square and all the evaluation and transposition identities. This proves the demanded realization normalization. It uses neither equality detection by finite evaluations nor invertibility of $\beta$ for arbitrary inputs; the integral Hom comparison is the ambient one already constructed.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: Rationalize the integral maps and their inverses. For arbitrary arrows $a=\sum_i a_i\otimes\lambda_i$ and $b=\sum_j b_j\otimes\nu_j$ in localized Hom groups, each naturality or evaluation equation expands by bilinearity to the integral equation for $(a_i,b_j)$ multiplied by $\lambda_i\nu_j$; similarly the transpose identity is linear in its input. The inverse identities and shift/composition identities localize as well. This proves the assertion for arbitrary rational morphisms, rather than just arrows which are integral. These are exactly the localized operations specified in the question.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: For a finite coefficient extension $E\subset L$, its completed coefficient sheaf is finite free over the original completed coefficient sheaf, and ordinary scalar extension agrees canonically with the specified completed one. The evaluation-normalized derived scalar adjunction identifies the restriction of $H_S(S\otimes_R^LM,S\otimes_R^LN)$ with $H_R(M,N\otimes_R^LS)$. On choosing a finite free basis for $S$, the latter is a finite direct sum of copies of $H_R(M,N)$: internal Hom preserves finite biproducts, either by its Hom-complex formula or by the transposition bijection. Therefore the scalar comparison is the direct sum of copies of Step 3's comparison, with evaluation $(f\otimes s)(x\otimes t)=f(x)\otimes st$. Reindexing fixes the coefficient scalars and hence commutes with this map. This argument uses finite direct sums only, so imposes no perfectness condition on the inputs. The formula is basis independent because it is the transpose of evaluation. It commutes with a further extension by associativity of scalar multiplication and tensor reassociation. The existing operation/scalar comparisons therefore carry $c$ to the comparison at the larger field, with its evaluation and shifts.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), enhanced by the stated resolution constructions

proof.text: Represent all objects, arrows and the comparisons over one common finite coefficient field in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Step 15 makes the class of $c$ independent of enlarging that field. If two arrow representatives become equal at a further field, their naturality equations and images under $c$ agree there, hence define equal classes. Evaluation, transposition, inverses, composition and shifts can each be checked at that common field using Steps 11 and 14; their classes have the required identities. This is precisely the common-stage operation construction, and completes all coefficient stages.
